teams.heading: Virimi Vakatawa scores but Fiji lose Pacific Nations Cup final to Japan
teams.body: Fiji surrendered their hold on the Pacific Nations Cup on Saturday as a late Samisoni Tua try snatched a 20-15 victory for Japan in Tokyo. Despite first-half tries from Virimi Vakatawa and hooker Tevita Ikanivere, the defending champions struggled with discipline after Mesake Doge's yellow card. Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula drew Fiji level with a late penalty, but the Flying Fijians could not withstand the late Japanese onslaught, falling just short of securing a third successive tournament title.

lead.why: Fiji's narrow defeat in the Pacific Nations Cup final is the weekend's biggest headline.

teams.heading: England and Canada share the spoils as historic winning run concludes
teams.body: England’s remarkable run of 39 successive victories has come to an end following a 26-26 draw against Canada at Sandy Park. Despite two first-half tries from Claudia Moloney-MacDonald, the Red Roses were unable to secure a win against a committed Canadian side who dominated the opening exchanges. Although England remain undefeated in 40 Tests, the result marks the first time since 2022 that they have failed to emerge victorious from an international fixture.

teams.heading: Ben Youngs claims France must defeat South Africa before World Cup

Writing on the For the Love of Rugby podcast, Youngs argued that failing to beat the world champions would leave a lasting psychological scar ahead of next year's World Cup. Fabien Galthié’s side are looking to address recent losses to the Springboks, including the narrow 29-28 defeat in the 2023 World Cup quarter-final.

teams.heading: World Rugby pushes USA proposal despite Six Nations stakeholder resistance reports
teams.body: World Rugby continues to advocate for moving a Six Nations fixture to the United States to broaden the sport's commercial reach, though the proposal faces significant internal hurdles. While reports from earlier this week indicate ongoing formal talks, the initiative remains in flux with stakeholders divided. The Irish Rugby Football Union has publicly registered its response to the plans, and other unions have expressed scepticism regarding the logistics. For now, the prospect of a championship match across the Atlantic remains unconfirmed.

teams.heading: Ceitidh Ainsworth earns first start as Sarah Bonar returns to squad
teams.body: Ceitidh Ainsworth makes her first start for Scotland Women against New Zealand following her debut off the bench in last weekend’s defeat by Canada. Interim head coach Dave Butcher has confirmed four changes for the WXV Global Series encounter at Hive Stadium, including the return of experienced lock Sarah Bonar. Returning from injury, the Harlequins forward is set to earn her 52nd cap from the bench as Scotland look to bounce back against the world-ranked opposition.

teams.heading: Wales beat South Africa as Sean Lynn hails side's new DNA
teams.body: Wales ended a nine-test winless run with a comprehensive 50-19 victory over South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park. A clinical attacking display saw the hosts cross for eight tries, including a double from Sisilia Tuipulotu, as Sean Lynn’s side flourished under the Friday night lights. The head coach praised his team’s execution, stating, “This is just the start for us, this is going to be our new DNA.” Co-captain Alex Callender was named player of the match in the emphatic win.

teams.heading: Les Kiss insists Australia can challenge the world champion Springboks side
teams.body: Wallabies coach Les Kiss has issued a defiant message ahead of next weekend's clash with South Africa, rejecting the notion that the world’s top-ranked side is untouchable. Kiss emphasised the importance of creative, unconventional rugby, suggesting his team is ready to embrace a fresh strategic approach. “It’s a massive opportunity to challenge a fantastic team that is second to none in the world,” said the coach. Australia head into this pivotal fixture looking to maintain momentum during their current unbeaten run.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones leads Japan to historic Pacific Nations Cup final victory
teams.body: Japan secured a hard-fought 20-15 victory over Fiji in Tokyo on Saturday to claim the Pacific Nations Cup title for the first time since 2019. After trailing at half-time, the Brave Blossoms rallied in the second period, with Mamoru Harada, Ben Gunter, and Samisoni Tua crossing for crucial tries. Eddie Jones hailed the result as a significant milestone, noting, “Our aim this weekend is to win the final and we’re 100 per cent concentrated on that.”

lead.why: Japan securing a historic Pacific Nations Cup title is the most significant development in the team's calendar today.

teams.heading: John Smit claims All Blacks must prioritise set-piece to compete globally
teams.body: Former Springboks captain John Smit has identified New Zealand’s scrum as a primary concern following their 3-1 series loss. Smit noted the All Blacks frequently opted for quick ball to avoid set-piece engagements, a trend he attributes to the differing priorities of Super Rugby compared to northern hemisphere competitions. Addressing the physical requirements of the modern game, Smit stated, “scrumming is like a UFC fighter. You can train in the gym as much as you want, but if you don’t put enough time in the ring.”

lead.why: This story captures the central tactical and structural challenge facing the team following the recent series against South Africa.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus releases Pieter-Steph du Toit and Damian de Allende early
teams.body: Coach Rassie Erasmus has confirmed that Pieter-Steph du Toit and Damian de Allende have been released from the Springbok squad ahead of the upcoming Test in Perth. Following a demanding series against the All Blacks, the pair will return to South Africa to spend time with their families. Erasmus stated that there is sufficient cover within the current travelling group to manage the squad's workload as the team shifts focus to their next assignment at the Optus Stadium.
